name: vn-en-eval-set-v3
description: VN→EN correction eval set v3 — 40 pairs targeting Stage-2 live categories: false-friend, calque, and medium-freq collocation (B1/B2 CEFR weighted). Zero duplicate inputs vs v1+v2 (case-insensitive).

entries.input: She is very sensible to other people's opinions and often gets upset.
entries.expected: She is very sensitive to other people's opinions and often gets upset.
entries.vietlishPattern: nhạy cảm → 'sensible' false-friend — Vietnamese 'nhạy cảm' = easily affected emotionally; English 'sensible' = having good practical judgment; 'sensitive' = easily affected; learner maps the L1 state adjective to the more familiar-looking English cognate

entries.input: He is a very considerable supervisor who always thinks about his team's wellbeing.
entries.expected: He is a very considerate supervisor who always thinks about his team's wellbeing.
entries.vietlishPattern: chu đáo/ân cần → 'considerable' false-friend — 'considerable' = large in amount or extent; 'considerate' = thoughtful toward others; Vietnamese 'chu đáo' has no exact cognate anchor so learner defaults to the longer-looking English adjective with the shared root

entries.input: She is the most industrial student I have ever taught.
entries.expected: She is the most industrious student I have ever taught.
entries.vietlishPattern: chăm chỉ/cần cù → 'industrial' false-friend — 'industrial' = relating to industry or manufacturing; 'industrious' = hardworking; the shared root 'industri-' traps learners who already know 'industrial revolution' and over-generalise the form to the person-adjective

entries.input: The city council made a historical decision to ban all single-use plastics.
entries.expected: The city council made a historic decision to ban all single-use plastics.
entries.vietlishPattern: quyết định lịch sử → 'historical' false-friend — 'historical' = relating to or about history; 'historic' = important or famous enough to be recorded in history; Vietnamese 'lịch sử' underdifferentiates the two; learners default to the longer, more common adjective form

entries.input: Can you tell me your actual phone number? I may have saved the old one.
entries.expected: Can you tell me your current phone number? I may have saved the old one.
entries.vietlishPattern: số điện thoại hiện tại → 'actual phone number' false-friend — Vietnamese 'hiện tại' = current/present; English 'actual' = real/genuine (not current); 'current' or 'present' is required to express the time sense; widespread false-friend in VN business and academic English

entries.input: My father is very economic and he always plans his expenses carefully.
entries.expected: My father is very economical and he always plans his expenses carefully.
entries.vietlishPattern: tiết kiệm/kinh tế → 'economic' false-friend — 'economic' = relating to the economy; 'economical' = cost-efficient or thrifty; Vietnamese 'kinh tế' can describe a frugal person; learner maps to the shorter, higher-frequency adjective rather than the person-quality form

entries.input: Can I lend your dictionary until tomorrow morning?
entries.expected: Can I borrow your dictionary until tomorrow morning?
entries.vietlishPattern: mượn → 'lend' vs 'borrow' false-friend — Vietnamese 'mượn' = take temporarily (borrow); English direction is reversed: 'lend' = give temporarily (what the owner does); 'borrow' = receive temporarily (what the requester does); directionality is absent in the L1 word

entries.input: I feel very sympathy for the children who lost their parents in the disaster.
entries.expected: I feel deep sympathy for the children who lost their parents in the disaster.
entries.vietlishPattern: rất đồng cảm → 'very sympathy' — Vietnamese 'đồng cảm' functions as adjective and noun; English 'sympathy' is a noun modified by adjectives like 'deep/great', not the adverb 'very'; false-friend between the noun and the adjectival sense; collocation: 'feel deep sympathy for'

entries.input: How do you call the small tool you use to open a bottle of wine?
entries.expected: What do you call the small tool you use to open a bottle of wine?
entries.vietlishPattern: cái này gọi là gì → 'how do you call' — Vietnamese question 'gọi là gì' (call is what); learner maps 'gì' (what) to 'how' by analogy with 'How do you say...?'; English naming question is 'What do you call...?' not 'How do you call...?'

entries.input: I always want to remind this rule when I write formal emails.
entries.expected: I always want to remember this rule when I write formal emails.
entries.vietlishPattern: nhắc nhở/nhớ → 'remind' used for self-recall — Vietnamese 'nhớ' covers both 'remember' (self-directed recall) and 'remind' (directing another person's attention); English 'remind' requires an external person object ('remind someone of something'); for self-directed recall, 'remember' is the correct verb

entries.input: She doesn't know to drive a car, so she always uses public transport.
entries.expected: She doesn't know how to drive a car, so she always uses public transport.
entries.vietlishPattern: không biết lái xe → 'know to drive' calque — Vietnamese 'biết + bare verb' (không biết lái); English requires 'know how to + verb'; 'how' is omitted in the direct calque because L1 'biết' immediately precedes the activity

entries.input: Do you know to make the traditional Vietnamese rice cake?
entries.expected: Do you know how to make the traditional Vietnamese rice cake?
entries.vietlishPattern: bạn có biết làm bánh chưng không → 'know to make' calque — same 'biết + verb' structure as above; 'know how to' is required; this is among the highest-frequency calques produced by Vietnamese learners at A2–B1

entries.input: There is rain outside, you should take an umbrella with you.
entries.expected: It is raining outside; you should take an umbrella with you.
entries.vietlishPattern: ngoài trời có mưa → 'there is rain' calque — Vietnamese existential 'có' + weather noun describes atmospheric conditions; English weather uses impersonal 'it' as dummy subject with progressive aspect ('it's raining'); 'there is rain' is a direct structural calque of the existential

entries.input: I feel not comfortable speaking in front of a large group of people.
entries.expected: I don't feel comfortable speaking in front of a large group of people.
entries.vietlishPattern: tôi cảm thấy không thoải mái → 'feel not comfortable' — Vietnamese negation 'không' is placed after the verb ('cảm thấy không'); English negation requires auxiliary 'don't' before the main verb; post-verbal 'not' is a direct calque of the L1 word order

entries.input: I have twenty-two years old and I am in my first year at university.
entries.expected: I am twenty-two years old and I am in my first year at university.
entries.vietlishPattern: tôi có hai mươi hai tuổi → 'have X years old' calque — Vietnamese possession verb 'có' (have) + number of years; English uses the copula 'be' for stating age ('I am'); one of the highest-frequency calques produced by Vietnamese beginners across all contexts

entries.input: His harsh words hurt in my heart and I felt very sad all day.
entries.expected: His harsh words hurt me deeply and I felt very sad all day.
entries.vietlishPattern: lời nói cay nghiệt của anh ấy làm đau lòng tôi → 'hurt in my heart' — Vietnamese 'đau lòng' (lòng = heart/inner feelings) is a fixed emotional expression; calqued as an anatomical location; English expresses this with a psychological subject and manner adverb: 'hurt me deeply'; body-part calque is a Stage-2B target

entries.input: How long you have been studying at this school?
entries.expected: How long have you been studying at this school?
entries.vietlishPattern: bạn học trường này bao lâu rồi → no subject-auxiliary inversion after 'how long' — Vietnamese appends 'bao lâu' at the end without structural change; English WH-question with present perfect requires auxiliary-subject inversion ('How long have you been...')

entries.input: He can able to communicate in English, French, and Japanese.
entries.expected: He can communicate in English, French, and Japanese.
entries.vietlishPattern: có thể → 'can able to' double modal — Vietnamese 'có thể' translates to both 'can' and 'be able to'; learner stacks both translations simultaneously; only one is needed: 'can communicate' or 'is able to communicate'

entries.input: He always must to check his messages before starting work in the morning.
entries.expected: He must always check his messages before starting work in the morning.
entries.vietlishPattern: anh ấy luôn phải kiểm tra → 'always must to' — Vietnamese 'phải' (must) directly precedes the verb in L1; learner inserts 'to' by analogy with 'have to/need to'; also places 'always' before 'must' (L1 adverb position); English: frequency adverb follows 'must'

entries.input: I want to make my English more better, so I practise every day.
entries.expected: I want to improve my English, so I practise every day.
entries.vietlishPattern: muốn làm tiếng Anh của tôi tốt hơn → 'make more better' — double comparative calque of 'tốt hơn' (more good); and 'làm X tốt hơn' SVOC calque; 'more better' is redundant (double comparative); English lexically encodes the improvement: 'improve my English'

entries.input: She is eating medicine three times a day as the doctor recommended.
entries.expected: She is taking medicine three times a day as the doctor recommended.
entries.vietlishPattern: ăn thuốc → 'eating medicine' — Vietnamese 'ăn thuốc' uses the eating verb for pills; 'uống thuốc' uses the drinking verb for liquids; English 'take medicine/tablets' is the fixed collocation regardless of form (pills, syrup, injection)

entries.input: He did a terrible mistake and had to apologise to the whole team.
entries.expected: He made a terrible mistake and had to apologise to the whole team.
entries.vietlishPattern: làm lỗi → 'did a mistake' — 'làm' (do/make) used for mistakes in Vietnamese; English fixed collocation: 'make a mistake', not 'do a mistake'; among the most frequent collocation errors in VN learner English corpora and a Stage-2A target

entries.input: All candidates must make the written exam before the practical test.
entries.expected: All candidates must take the written exam before the practical test.
entries.vietlishPattern: dự thi/làm bài thi → 'make the exam' — Vietnamese 'làm bài thi' (do the exam paper) or 'dự thi' (attend the exam); English: candidates 'take' (sit) an exam; 'make' implies creating or constructing, not sitting; 'take an exam/test' is the standard collocation

entries.input: She gave birth a healthy baby girl this morning.
entries.expected: She gave birth to a healthy baby girl this morning.
entries.vietlishPattern: sinh một bé gái khoẻ mạnh → 'give birth a baby' — Vietnamese 'sinh + object' is transitive with no preposition needed; English 'give birth to' is a fixed phrasal collocation requiring 'to' before the noun; omitting 'to' produces an ungrammatical string

entries.input: I have a very strong headache and cannot focus on my work at all.
entries.expected: I have a very bad headache and cannot focus on my work at all.
entries.vietlishPattern: đau đầu rất mạnh → 'strong headache' — Vietnamese 'mạnh' (strong/intense) intensifies pain; English collocates pain and ache with 'bad/terrible/splitting/severe', not 'strong'; 'strong' collocates with sensory intensity (strong smell) or physical force, not bodily pain

entries.input: We lost a lot of time stuck in traffic and missed the opening of the show.
entries.expected: We wasted a lot of time stuck in traffic and missed the opening of the show.
entries.vietlishPattern: mất nhiều thời gian → 'lost time' — Vietnamese 'mất' covers both 'lose' (be deprived of) and 'waste' (spend poorly); English distinguishes: 'lose time' = time taken away uncontrollably; 'waste time' = time spent unproductively; being stuck in traffic is 'wasting', not 'losing'

entries.input: He works very hard and wins a lot of money from his business every year.
entries.expected: He works very hard and earns a lot of money from his business every year.
entries.vietlishPattern: kiếm được nhiều tiền → 'wins money' — Vietnamese 'được tiền' (get/receive money) or 'kiếm tiền' (earn money); English 'win' applies to competitions with an opponent; regular income or profit from business is always 'earned', not 'won'

entries.input: Please make your best to complete this task before five o'clock.
entries.expected: Please do your best to complete this task before five o'clock.
entries.vietlishPattern: cố hết sức → 'make your best' — Vietnamese 'làm hết sức' (make/do all effort); English fixed idiom is 'do your best' (not 'make your best'); cf. 'make an effort' and 'do your best' require different verbs; 'make' and 'do' collocations are a high-yield correction target

entries.input: They made a research on the buying behaviour of young consumers last year.
entries.expected: They conducted research on the buying behaviour of young consumers last year.
entries.vietlishPattern: làm/tiến hành nghiên cứu → 'made a research' — 'research' is uncountable; 'a research' is ungrammatical; standard collocations: 'conduct/carry out/do research' with no article; 'làm nghiên cứu' produces 'make + a + research' by analogy with countable task nouns

entries.input: All staff members must do a health check every six months.
entries.expected: All staff members must have a health check every six months.
entries.vietlishPattern: khám sức khoẻ → 'do a health check' — Vietnamese 'làm/đi khám' (do/go for a check); English: the patient 'has/undergoes' a medical check (receives it as a service); the doctor or clinic 'does/performs' it; learner assigns the active role to the wrong party

entries.input: She opened her eyes big when she heard the news.
entries.expected: She opened her eyes wide when she heard the news.
entries.vietlishPattern: mắt mở to → 'opened eyes big' — Vietnamese 'to' (big/large) is the correct modifier for widely-opened eyes in L1; English collocates 'open + eyes + wide'; 'wide' is the fixed manner adverb for aperture ('wide open', 'eyes wide', 'gaping wide')

entries.input: There is a heavy problem with the new software that we need to fix urgently.
entries.expected: There is a serious problem with the new software that we need to fix urgently.
entries.vietlishPattern: vấn đề nặng/nghiêm trọng → 'heavy problem' — Vietnamese 'nặng' (heavy/grave) modifies serious situations; English 'heavy' collocates with physical weight, traffic ('heavy traffic'), or rain ('heavy rain'); 'problem/issue' takes 'serious/major/significant', not 'heavy'

entries.input: She studied English for two hours before going to bed last night.
entries.expected: She studied English for two hours before going to bed last night.
entries.vietlishPattern: acceptable: 'for + duration' in past context is correct; 'before going to bed' is a natural adjunct; no correction needed

entries.input: I would appreciate it if you could send me the updated file by tomorrow.
entries.expected: I would appreciate it if you could send me the updated file by tomorrow.
entries.vietlishPattern: acceptable: 'would appreciate it if you could' is a correct formal hedged request; 'by tomorrow' correctly marks a deadline; no correction needed

entries.input: He not only passed the exam but also achieved the highest score in the class.
entries.expected: He not only passed the exam but also achieved the highest score in the class.
entries.vietlishPattern: acceptable: 'not only...but also' without fronting is grammatical when the subject precedes 'not only'; no auxiliary inversion needed here; no correction needed

entries.input: Despite the heavy workload, she managed to submit all her assignments on time.
entries.expected: Despite the heavy workload, she managed to submit all her assignments on time.
entries.vietlishPattern: acceptable: 'despite + noun phrase' (not 'despite of'); 'managed to + infinitive' is correctly formed; 'heavy workload' is a natural collocation; no correction needed

entries.input: She is very talent and can draw beautiful portraits in just one hour.
entries.expected: She is very talented and can draw beautiful portraits in just one hour.
entries.vietlishPattern: rất tài năng → 'very talent' false-friend — Vietnamese 'tài năng' functions as both noun and adjective; English 'talent' is a noun only; the adjective form is 'talented' (past-participial adjective); learner uses the noun in the adjective slot, a sub-type of the noun/adjective false-friend pattern

entries.input: He drinks very much beer every evening and it is affecting his health.
entries.expected: He drinks a lot of beer every evening and it is affecting his health.
entries.vietlishPattern: uống rất nhiều bia → 'drinks very much beer' — Vietnamese 'rất nhiều' (very many/much) maps directly to 'very much'; English 'very much' modifies verbs ('thank you very much') or predicates, not nouns; 'a lot of' is the standard informal quantifier for large quantities before nouns

entries.input: The team made a very big progress during the last quarter.
entries.expected: The team made very good progress during the last quarter.
entries.vietlishPattern: tiến bộ rất lớn → 'a very big progress' — 'progress' is uncountable; 'a progress' is ungrammatical; also 'big' is not the standard collocate: English uses 'good/significant/remarkable/considerable progress'; learner applies the Vietnamese size modifier 'lớn' (big/large) directly

entries.input: The company must catch more customers if it wants to grow in this competitive market.
entries.expected: The company must attract more customers if it wants to grow in this competitive market.
entries.vietlishPattern: thu hút/bắt khách hàng → 'catch customers' — Vietnamese 'bắt' (catch/grab) or 'thu hút' (attract/draw in); English 'catch' collocates with fish, balls, buses, or illnesses — not customers; standard business collocations: 'attract/win/gain customers'
